title: One calm inbox
caption: All Inboxes gathers every account into one list, with unread dots, VIP stars, flags, thread counts and a colour stripe that tells you which account each message came to.
alt: Loupe's All Inboxes list in light mode. Rows from Jordan Lee (Re: Dinner Saturday?, Photos from Sunday’s hike), Tracker, Dana Okafor (RE: Atlas Q4 roadmap review), Felix Brandt and Ben Walsh, each with sender, time, subject and a two-line preview; blue unread dots, VIP stars, orange flags, thread counts and blue, orange and teal account stripes down the left edge. A bottom bar reads Updated Just Now, 17 Unread.

title: Readable mode
caption: Marketing mail is reflowed into clean, phone-sized reading with its pictures and buttons intact, and the trackers it carries are counted right next to the sender.
alt: A Trailhead Outfitters newsletter, “Members: 20% off layers + the autumn layering guide”, open in Readable mode: a green verified-sender shield and a tracker count of 1 beside the sender, a purple Later tag, the Trailhead logo, a sunset hero image captioned “Into the cold.”, the heading “Three layers, every trail.”, body text and a green Shop the guide button. The reading toolbar sits at the bottom.

title: Search that understands
caption: Type a search expression, Thunderbird style, and Loupe highlights it and explains it as chips you can edit, so precise searches stay readable.
alt: The search screen with the expression f:(dana or ben) -is:read typed in, its operators coloured. Below it two chips read “From: dana or ben” and “Unread”, then 4 Results with a Save as Smart Mailbox button: unread messages from Dana Okafor and Ben Walsh, each showing its mailbox and account (Inbox · Work).

title: Search as you type
caption: While you type an expression, Loupe explains each part as a chip, suggests what can come next with an example, and shows the matching mail right away.
alt: The search screen while typing f:(dana or ben) is:unread a, with the cursor after the last letter. Chips below the field read “From: dana or ben”, “Unread” and “a”. Under them, suggestions complete the word being typed: attachment: (e.g. attachment:yes), after: (e.g. after:2026-03-01), all: (e.g. all:weekend) and account: (e.g. account:work). Then 4 Results with a Save as Smart Mailbox button, starting with unread mail from Dana Okafor and Ben Walsh.

title: Phishing, explained
caption: When a message looks like phishing, Loupe turns its links off and tells you why in plain words, instead of just showing a scary warning.
alt: A sheet titled “This looks like phishing” over a message from “Northwind IT” marked Possible phishing. Under WHY it lists “Look-alike domain: northwlnd.example looks like your own domain, northwind.example, but it is a different domain” and “Uses the name of someone you know”, explaining that the sender is new and replies would go to yet another address, with advice to check another way first.

title: Three panes on tablets
caption: On a tablet in landscape, mailboxes, the message list and the open message sit side by side, so you can triage without losing your place.
alt: Loupe on a landscape tablet in three panes: Mailboxes on the left (All Inboxes, VIP, Flagged, Unread, Snoozed, Subscriptions and the Personal account’s folders), All Inboxes in the middle with “Photos from Sunday’s hike” selected, and that message on the right with Jordan Lee’s note and a photo carousel showing a purple mountain sunset.

title: Unsubscribe centre
caption: Subscriptions lists every newsletter with how often it arrives and how much of it you actually read, so leaving the ones you ignore is a tap away.
alt: The Subscriptions screen on its Newsletters tab (a Discussions tab beside it), with a filter field and Never Read 5, Rarely Read 5 and All 10 chips. Rows for MegaMart Deals, Tidepool, Stride Run Club, Nordlicht Books, Northline Rail, Tracker and Lumen Bank show the sender address, a rate such as “≈ 3 / month · read 0%” and an Unsubscribe button.

title: Smart Mailboxes
caption: Save any search as a Smart Mailbox that sits next to your folders, and fold away the accounts you don’t need to see.
alt: The Mailboxes screen: All Inboxes 17, VIP 4, Flagged 6, Unread 39, Snoozed 3 and Subscriptions 5, then the folded accounts Personal, Work and Fastmail, each with a coloured dot, and a Smart Mailboxes section with Receipts & Invoices and Big Attachments.

title: Invitations, answered
caption: Meeting invitations show as a card above the message, with the time in both time zones, the join link and Accept, Maybe and Decline right there.
alt: An Outlook invitation from Olivia Grant shown as a card titled “SOW phase 2 – pricing review”: a date next week, 9:00–10:00 AM Los Angeles and 5:00–6:00 PM your time, a Teams meeting with a Join button, Olivia Grant as organizer, 3 guests with 1 accepted, Accept, Maybe and Decline buttons, a note on where the reply goes, and Add a Comment and Add to Calendar links. The meeting text follows below.

title: Encrypted, verified
caption: OpenPGP and S/MIME mail is decrypted and checked on your phone, compatible with Thunderbird, with a clear summary of who signed it and what was protected.
alt: A sheet titled “Signed by Dana Okafor” with a green check badge, saying only you and the other recipients can read the message and the signature is valid. ENCRYPTION: Decrypted on this device, with the key IDs, and Protected subject “Offsite venue (confidential)”. SIGNATURE: Dana Okafor’s address, her key fingerprint, the signing date, Acceptance “Accepted and verified” and a Change Acceptance button. A footer says it was checked on this device with OpenPGP, compatible with Thunderbird.

title: Writing a message
caption: A focused compose screen with recipient chips, the identity you send from, and Send Later one tap away.
alt: The compose screen for a message titled “Lisbon in November” to Jordan Lee and Priya Nair, shown as chips. Cc and Bcc are empty, the From line reads Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@gmail.example>, and the body is a short note about flights, a flat in Alfama and a Sintra day trip. The top bar has Cancel, Attach, Send Later and a blue Send button.

title: Rules in plain search
caption: Write a rule the way you search, choose what it does, and run it on the phone or on your mail server as a Sieve script you can read.
alt: The New Rule editor: the condition from:@brandt.example with a “From: @brandt.example” chip, a hint to write it as you would search, Accounts set to Fastmail, the action Mark as Read with Add Action below, a Stop Processing More Rules switch, Run On set to Server rather than This Device, and the generated Sieve script shown in a monospaced box.

title: Patches as diffs
caption: For technical mailing lists, Loupe shows plain text in a monospaced font and renders patches as coloured diffs, like reading a pull request.
alt: A Kestrel developers list message from Ines Duarte, “[PATCH v2 2/3] http: reuse cached headers on keep-alive connections”, in a monospaced font. A “1 file changed +9 −4” summary leads into a diff of src/http.c with line numbers, blue hunk headers, removed lines in red and added lines in green.
